title: Playtest script authoring job
description: One bounded authoring job: a target the owner authorized, where its OpenAPI document comes from, the rule statements they approved, and the budgets the loop may spend. See docs/contracts/scripts.md#the-authoring-loop.

target.description: The one API this job authors against.

base_url.description: The target's base URL. Every path a script uses is appended to it, and its origin is the only one the client may reach by default.

allowed_origins.description: Extra origins the client may reach besides base_url's own — bare http(s) origins, same semantics as the API driver's egress allowlist. A credential reference never resolves for one of these.

authorization.description: The recorded target authorization (DESIGN §4 step 2): the owner's answer to "safe to write test data to this environment?". Authoring refuses to start without it, and it covers exactly the origin it names — an origin change invalidates it.

origin.description: The origin this authorization covers. It must be base_url's origin.

approved_by.description: Who declared it. An authorization records a person, not a flag.

record.description: Where the declaration is written down — a document path or a URL.

write.description: Whether the owner authorized writes. false keeps the client in read-only mode: only GET and HEAD are forwarded, at the wire.

spec.description: Where the OpenAPI document comes from. Omit it to auto-discover the document on the target. There is no way to declare that a job has no spec: every operation obligation comes from the document.

oneOf.description: A local path, or an http(s) URL.

file.description: A path to the document, resolved relative to this file.

url.description: An http(s) URL the document is fetched from.

document.description: The document itself, pasted or uploaded.

text.description: The document as JSON or YAML text.

discover.description: Probe the target for the document (the default when nothing else is named).

paths.description: Override the conventional paths auto-discovery probes, e.g. ["/openapi.json", "/swagger.json"].

rules.description: The approved rule statements. Only sentences a human approved reach a handout or a gate. Until rule cards ship (S3), this is a hand-written list or an INVARIANTS.md document.

oneOf.description: A path to an INVARIANTS.md (or .json) document, resolved relative to this file.

id.description: The rule's obligation id becomes rule:<id>. Derived from the title or statement when omitted.

statement.description: The approved sentence, exactly as the owner approved it.

applicability.description: Where the rule applies, and its declared exceptions.

notes.description: The owner's notes on the card. They steer authoring and appear in the handout beside their rule.

approved_skip_reasons.description: Reasons a suite may cite to leave this obligation uncovered. Any other reason leaves it unaccounted, which is unsound.

unsupported.description: The owner marked this rule as inexpressible on this substrate.

provenance.description: Where the card came from, e.g. "POST /transfers · status enum".

secrets.description: The PLAYTEST_SECRET_<NAME> references this job permits. A script can cause an authenticated request with one; it can never read the value.

role.description: Who this credential authenticates, as one line in the handout. What it can reach is for the author to discover.

params.description: A frozen JSON object handed to the script. It must never carry a secret reference.

reset.description: The target's reset affordance, in one sentence, e.g. "POST /admin/reset with {\"seed\":\"dev\"} restores the seeded state". Stated in the handout so every execution starts from a known state.

model.description: The model that authors. Defaults to the configured actor model.

out_dir.description: Where the handout, executions, transcript, and bundle are written. Resolved relative to this file.

budget.description: Three ceilings, all enforced. Defaults are productized from what the S0 trials actually used (docs/contracts/scripts.md#authoring-budgets).

iterations.description: Model turns for the whole job (default 8).

requests.description: Requests across every execution of the job (default 1500).

wall_clock_ms.description: Wall clock for the whole job (default 2700000 — 45 minutes).

execution_budget.description: Wire-enforced request budget for one execution (default 400).

max_output_tokens.description: Output ceiling for one model turn. A whole suite comes back every turn, so this is large by default (64000).
